stages.name: Not yet on his road
stages.desc: Rousseau has not yet lived in or passed through this region

stages.name: On his road
stages.desc: He has lived here or travelled through, and moved on

stages.name: His home
stages.desc: Where he lives in this year

stages.name: Closed to him
stages.desc: His book burned and his arrest ordered: he cannot safely live here

stages.name: Hiding place
stages.desc: He shelters here under a protector, often under a false name

states.name: Hauts-de-France
timeline: Picardy and the Oise valley
The château of Trye, near Gisors: hidden by the Prince of Conti as 'Monsieur Renou'
He leaves Trye in June, convinced he is watched
Ermenonville: a cottage on the Marquis de Girardin's estate; he dies there on 2 July

states.name: Grand Est
timeline: Alsace, Lorraine and Champagne
Strasbourg welcomes him for a month on his way from Switzerland to Paris

states.name: Provence-Alpes-Côte-d'Azur
timeline: Provence: never on Rousseau's road

states.name: Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes
timeline: Lyon and Dauphiné are French; Savoy (Annecy, Chambéry) belongs to the King of Sardinia
Annecy, in Savoy: the runaway reaches Madame de Warens
Chambéry, in Savoy: he lives with Madame de Warens, whom he calls Maman
Les Charmettes, a house outside Chambéry: years of reading, music and botany
Lyon: tutor to the two sons of Monsieur de Mably
He leaves for Paris with a new system for writing music
Grenoble, then Bourgoin, under the name Renou; he marries Thérèse at Bourgoin in August
Monquin, a farmhouse in the hills above Bourgoin
He leaves the Dauphiné for Paris

states.name: Nouvelle-Aquitaine
timeline: Guyenne, Poitou and Limousin: never on Rousseau's road

states.name: Occitanie
timeline: Languedoc
Montpellier: he travels there to consult the doctors

states.name: Bourgogne-Franche-Comté
timeline: Burgundy and Franche-Comté
The Academy of Dijon awards its prize to his first discourse

states.name: Pays de la Loire
timeline: Anjou, Maine and the lower Loire: never on Rousseau's road

states.name: Bretagne
timeline: Brittany: never on Rousseau's road

states.name: Normandie
timeline: Normandy: Trye lies just over its border, near Gisors

states.name: Corse
timeline: Corsica, ruled by the Republic of Genoa
Pasquale Paoli leads an independent Corsican government
A Corsican officer asks Rousseau to draft laws for the island
France conquers Corsica, ending the project

states.name: Centre-Val de Loire
timeline: The Loire valley
Chenonceau: secretary to the Dupin family at their château on the Cher

states.name: Île-de-France
timeline: Paris, capital of the King of France
A first visit, on foot; he finds the city dirty and disappointing
He settles in Paris and presents his music system to the Academy of Sciences
He leaves for Venice as an ambassador's secretary
Back in Paris; in 1745 he meets Thérèse Levasseur
The walk to Vincennes, and the prize question
The Hermitage, a cottage in the woods of Montmorency
He breaks with Diderot and Madame d'Épinay and moves to Mont-Louis, in Montmorency
The Parlement of Paris condemns Émile to be burned and orders his arrest; he flees
Back in Paris, tolerated if he publishes nothing; he copies music in the rue Plâtrière
In May he leaves Paris for Ermenonville

events.title: Born in Geneva
events.text: Jean-Jacques is born on 28 June in the Grand-Rue, son of the watchmaker Isaac Rousseau; his mother dies nine days later.

events.title: Father flees
events.text: After a quarrel with a French officer, Isaac Rousseau leaves Geneva to avoid prison and settles at Nyon.

events.title: Bossey parsonage
events.text: Jean-Jacques and his cousin board with Pastor Lambercier in the village of Bossey.

events.title: Locked out
events.text: On Sunday 14 March he finds the city gates shut for the third time, and leaves Geneva.

events.title: Madame de Warens
events.text: In Annecy he meets Françoise-Louise de Warens, a convert paid to bring Protestants into the Catholic Church.

events.title: Baptised in Turin
events.text: At Turin's hospice for converts he abjures Protestantism and is baptised a Catholic in April.

events.title: The stolen ribbon
events.text: A servant in Turin, he steals a ribbon and blames a young maid, Marion; he confesses it decades later.

events.title: Music teacher
events.text: Penniless, he teaches music in Lausanne under an invented name, Vaussore de Villeneuve.

events.title: First sight of Paris
events.text: He walks to Paris for a post as a servant and is disappointed by its dirty streets.

events.title: Chambéry
events.text: He rejoins Madame de Warens in Chambéry, capital of Savoy.

events.title: Les Charmettes
events.text: Summers at a country house above Chambéry: he reads philosophy, music and science on his own.

events.title: Montpellier
events.text: Believing himself mortally ill, he travels to Montpellier to consult its doctors.

events.title: Tutor in Lyon
events.text: He becomes tutor to the sons of Monsieur de Mably, and fails at it.

events.title: Music by numbers
events.text: He presents a system of writing music with numbers to the Academy of Sciences, which finds it neither new nor useful.

events.title: Venice
events.text: Secretary to the French ambassador, the Comte de Montaigu; after a bitter quarrel he leaves in August 1744.

events.title: Thérèse Levasseur
events.text: At his lodging house he meets Thérèse Levasseur, a linen maid; she stays with him for life.

events.title: Foundling hospital
events.text: The first of five children he has with Thérèse is left at the foundling hospital; the other four follow.

events.title: Chenonceau
events.text: Secretary to the Dupin family, he spends an autumn at their château on the Cher.

events.title: Road to Vincennes
events.text: Walking to see Diderot in prison, he reads the Academy of Dijon's prize question.

events.title: Prize at Dijon
events.text: His Discourse on the Sciences and Arts, arguing that they have not improved morals, wins the prize.

events.title: The Village Soothsayer
events.text: His one-act opera is performed before Louis XV at Fontainebleau on 18 October.

events.title: Citizen again
events.text: In Geneva he returns to the Protestant church and regains his citizenship.

events.title: Discourse on Inequality
events.text: Published in Amsterdam by Marc-Michel Rey: inequality is born of society, not nature.

events.title: The Hermitage
events.text: Madame d'Épinay lends him a cottage in the woods of Montmorency.

events.title: Julie
events.text: His novel in letters, Julie, or the New Heloise, becomes a best-seller.

events.title: The Social Contract
events.text: Published in Amsterdam in April: 'Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.'

events.title: Émile burned
events.text: On 9 June the Parlement of Paris condemns Émile and orders his arrest; the book is burned at the Palais de Justice.

events.title: Geneva burns both
events.text: On 19 June Geneva's Small Council orders Émile and The Social Contract burned, and his arrest if he enters.

events.title: Expelled from Yverdon
events.text: He takes refuge at Yverdon, but Bern, which rules the town, orders him out in July.

events.title: Môtiers
events.text: In the Val de Travers he lives under the protection of the King of Prussia, wearing a long Armenian robe.

events.title: No longer a citizen
events.text: In May he renounces his citizenship of Geneva.

events.title: Voltaire's pamphlet
events.text: An anonymous pamphlet by Voltaire reveals to the public that Rousseau abandoned his children.

events.title: Laws for Corsica
events.text: Invited to draft a constitution for independent Corsica, he begins a project he never finishes.

events.title: Stones at Môtiers
events.text: On the night of 6 September villagers stone his house after sermons against him.

events.title: Island of Saint-Pierre
events.text: Six weeks of happiness on an island in Lake Biel, until Bern expels him again.

events.title: Strasbourg
events.text: On his way out of Switzerland, the city welcomes him for a month.

events.title: London with Hume
events.text: On 13 January he reaches London with David Hume, who has found him a refuge.

events.title: Wootton Hall
events.text: From March he lives at Wootton in Staffordshire; in July he accuses Hume of plotting against him.

events.title: Flight from England
events.text: In May he sails from Dover back to France.

events.title: Trye
events.text: The Prince of Conti hides him at the château of Trye under the name Renou.

events.title: Married at Bourgoin
events.text: After twenty-three years together, he marries Thérèse in a ceremony of his own devising.

events.title: Rue Plâtrière
events.text: Settled in Paris, he earns his living copying music and botanises on long walks.

events.title: Knocked down
events.text: On 24 October a Great Dane running ahead of a carriage knocks him down at Ménilmontant.

events.title: Voltaire dies
events.text: His great rival dies in Paris on 30 May.

events.title: Ermenonville
events.text: He dies on 2 July and is buried on the Isle of Poplars in the park.

chartNote: Share of the area of today's metropolitan France, by what each present-day region was to Rousseau in that year. A whole region takes the colour of one town or house in it. Savoy (Annecy, Chambéry) belonged to the King of Sardinia until 1860 and is shown in its present region. Geneva, Turin, Neuchâtel, Bern, Venice and England lie outside the coloured map; his years there appear as events.
